extracted.intended_audience: established investigators, institutional PD/PIs, and research administrators preparing NIH Institutional (T-series) training grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for institutions/applicants seeking NIH Institutional (T-series) training awards (NRSA and related activity codes), covering program scope, eligible applicants and trainees, allowable costs, appointment/selection, review criteria pointer, and applicable policy notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program scope / eligible institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional training programs (often referred to as the 'T' series) provide domestic, nonprofit, and private or public graduate-level academic institutions with funds for research training opportunities, including international, for trainees at the undergraduate, graduate, and postdoctoral levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should come from eligible domestic graduate-level academic institutions (public or private, nonprofit). Programs may include international research training opportunities for trainees. See the Explore NIH Grant Opportunities tool to find appropriate T-series FOAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible applicants / Training PD/PI
rubrics_metrics.description: Established investigators who lead research or training programs at an institution are eligible to apply for these grants. Established investigators are typically designated as the Training Program Director/Principal Investigator (Training PD/PI) to oversee training programs for their institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards are made to institutions; the Training PD/PI oversees training, mentoring, recruitment of trainees, and program administration. Ensure the PD/PI meets the FOA's definition of 'established investigator' and institutional authorization is in place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and program goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards are made to institutions for investigators to recruit a cohort of trainees who participate in organized approaches to biomedical research training, mentoring and career development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should describe structured training activities, mentoring plans, career development components, and cohort recruitment strategies. Emphasize organized, programmatic approaches rather than individual fellowships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable costs and support to trainees
rubrics_metrics.description: Training grants offset the cost of stipends, tuition and fees, and training related expenses, including health insurance, for the appointed trainees in accordance with the approved NIH support levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget requests must conform to NIH/NRSA stipend levels, tuition/fee caps, and policies. Consult current NRSA stipend levels and related NIH policy notices when preparing budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trainee appointment and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainee-level investigators should contact their institution about training opportunities. Appointees to these training programs are selected by the PD/PI of an awarded grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application should describe appointment procedures, selection criteria, and responsibilities of the PD/PI in selecting and appointing trainees. Trainee recruitment and appointment processes should align with institutional and NIH requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trainee levels and definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs may support Undergraduate Trainees, Predoctoral Trainees, and Postdoctoral/Residency Trainees. Definitions: Undergraduate (bachelor's or equivalent period); Predoctoral (period pursuing research doctorate); Postdoctoral (temporary mentored advanced training after doctoral degree); Residency (GME providing hands-on specialty training).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the appropriate activity code and tailor training plans to the trainee level(s) supported. Clarify eligibility criteria for each trainee category in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity codes and program types
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional training award activity codes referenced include: Undergraduate NRSA Institutional Research Training Grant (T34); Interdisciplinary Research Training Award (T90) and combined Research Education Grant (R90); Institutional NRSA (T32); NRSA Short-Term Research Training (T35); Mentored Research Pathway in Residency (R38); Dissertation Award (R36); International Research Training Grant (D43).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the activity code that matches the trainee level and program design. The page lists activity codes by trainee level and program type — applicants must follow the FOA-specific instructions for the chosen activity code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review criteria and where to find them
rubrics_metrics.description: To find the criteria reviewers will use to evaluate your application, see Section V of your funding opportunity. Parent Announcements include the minimum standard review criteria appropriate for their program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review criteria are FOA-specific; consult Section V of the FOA (or the Research Training Parent Announcements) for the precise reviewer criteria and scoring guidance to address in your application.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRSA program status and changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The majority of NIH-funded training awards are through the Ruth L. Kirschstein National Research Service Award (NRSA) program. NRSA Training Program applications have undergone changes that impact the NRSA Training Tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of recent and forthcoming NRSA policy and form changes (e.g., revisions to application and review processes). Review linked NOTs (policy notices) and the 'Learn more' resources to ensure compliance with updated requirements and training tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative supplements and additional funding opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: An administrative supplement is a non-competing award that provides additional funding to a currently funded grant. NIH participates in funding opportunities for specific programs (e.g., Research Supplements to Promote Re-entry & Re-integration into Health-Related Research Careers; Research Continuity Supplements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current T awardees should monitor administrative supplement opportunities for eligibility and application procedures. Administrative supplements are program-specific and are awarded as non-competing increments to existing grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy compliance (stipends, childcare, application/review process)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and awards must comply with NIH policies (examples cited: NRSA stipend levels, procedures for childcare costs for NRSA Institutional Research Training Awards, updates to application and review process for fellowships and institutional awards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the listed policy notices (e.g., NOT-OD-25-100, NOT-OD-24-129, NOT-OD-24-116, NOT-OD-24-107, NOT-OD-24-084, NOT-OD-23-111) and ensure application materials and budgets conform to the current NIH/AHRQ/NRSA policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program design: cohort-based, multi-lab inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: These training awards provide individual research training opportunities (including international) to trainees at the undergraduate, graduate, and postdoctoral levels and can include trainees from multiple different labs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design applications to support cohorts possibly spanning multiple laboratories or departments; detail mentoring structures, cross-lab coordination, and how the program will provide cohesive training despite multi-lab appointments.
